hero_description: Backend developer focused on Java and Spring Boot, transitioning from game programming. I apply my experience in game systems and multiplayer networking to build clean, structured, and well-tested APIs.
about_bio:
Hi, I am Márcio Rosendo Filho. Graduated in Digital Games Technology, my path began in Game Development, where I designed real-time gameplay architectures, state machines, and multiplayer networking topologies (Photon PUN, WebSockets with Go backends) in Unity (C#). Managing real-time systems built my experience in resource allocation, latency tuning, and editor automation.

Today, I apply these skills to backend development. I build REST APIs with Java 17 and Spring Boot, using Spring Data JPA for database modeling, Flyway for schema migration, and Spring Security with JWT for authentication.

My focus is on clean, secure code. I implement automated unit and integration tests in CI/CD pipelines, design layered architectures, and use immutable structures for data transfer.

project1_description: Contributed as a Backend and Game Programmer on a live browser RPG, developing gameplay mechanics, integrating WebSocket client-server communication, and managing Docker deployments.
project1_challenge: Implementing WebSocket integration with a Go backend for real-time game state synchronization and server-side data validation on a live codebase, while handling cloud infrastructure and routing configuration.
project1_features: Implemented WebSocket client-server communication with a Go backend for real-time game state synchronization and data validation.
Built business logic features including cloud-persisted inventory, card collections, and weighted probability systems for drop rates and enchantments.
Developed internal Unity editor tools for structured data validation and bulk CSV/ScriptableObject export pipelines, automating repetitive design team tasks.
Configured Docker containers, Nginx reverse proxies, Cloudflare routing, and GCP VM instances for application deployments.
project2_description: A 3D multiplayer co-op game developed by an 8-person team. Originally created as a capstone project (TCC), the project was subsequently extended through the Sampa Games (Spcine) development grant and selected for exhibition in the Student Panorama at Gamescom LATAM 2025.
project2_challenge: One multiplayer puzzle featured several physics-driven interactables with chained states. The problem was not just syncing transforms; it was ensuring correct network ownership at the exact moment of interaction, otherwise both clients could apply authority simultaneously and diverge. Solved with a staged bootstrap and handshake: each client reports ready after local setup, the host then assigns ownership deterministically and only then enables puzzle initialization and sync, eliminating race conditions under latency.
project2_features: Implemented the lobby and room system using Photon PUN, integrating Steam profiles via SDK.
Developed level-specific multiplayer mechanics and synchronized co-op interactions.
Solved network ownership race conditions through a staged bootstrap and deterministic host-side handshake.
Extended capstone project under the Sampa Games (Spcine) development grant.
Selected for exhibition at Gamescom LATAM 2025 (Student Panorama).
project3_description: A 3D psychological horror escape room game developed over a four-month period. Acted as Producer and Programmer.
project3_challenge: Designing a state-driven finite state machine (FSM) for enemy AI to translate sound events into deterministic transitions, optimizing execution time within the game loop.
project3_features: Managed project scope, timelines, and team coordination in the role of Producer.
Implemented state-based enemy AI systems featuring player-generated sound detection (steps, doors, and interactions).
Created event-driven interaction systems connected to enemy awareness mechanics.
project4_description: A comedic 2D narrative puzzle game developed over a four-month period. Acted as the main programmer, building the gameplay systems, user interface, and narrative integration from scratch.
project4_challenge: Implementing a modular room and wall inspection flow that tracks puzzle state changes and integrates branching narrative beats using the Fungus dialogue engine.
project4_features: Developed core 2D gameplay systems, interaction logic, and room/wall navigation flows.
Built the complete user interface and menu system.
Integrated the Fungus engine to drive dynamic dialogue trees and localized voice-over playback.

project5_subtitle: REST API with verified reviews, JWT auth, and CI/CD • 05/2026 - 06/2026
project5_description: Marketplace REST API developed to ensure product reviews are submitted exclusively by verified buyers. Developed with Java 17, Spring Boot 3.x, and PostgreSQL.
project5_challenge: Securing critical endpoints using UUIDs against ID enumeration attacks, managing database versioning with Flyway while implementing Soft Delete logic to preserve historical data, and establishing integration tests using Testcontainers in a GitHub Actions pipeline.
project5_features: Implemented JWT authentication and authorization using Spring Security with UUID-based endpoints to prevent ID enumeration attacks.
Modeled relational database schemas using Spring Data JPA, managed versioning via Flyway, and implemented Soft Delete logic to preserve historical data and maintain referential integrity.
Developed unit and integration test suites using Testcontainers to validate database operations against an ephemeral PostgreSQL instance inside GitHub Actions.
project6_subtitle: Java Spring Boot API featuring Bean Validation and immutable records • 05/2026 - 05/2026
project6_description: REST API for task management, implemented to showcase clean layered architecture, input validation, and best practices in API design using Java 17, Spring Boot 3, and H2 Database.
project6_challenge: Ensuring payload immutability across application layers and standardizing API error responses through centralized exception handling while enforcing declarative validation rules.
project6_features: Structured controllers, services, and repositories to guarantee strict separation of concerns and database decoupling.
Ensured entry and exit payload immutability through Java Record DTOs.
Implemented centralized exception handling (ControllerAdvice) to standardize API error responses.
Applied declarative data validation rules using Bean Validation and documented APIs using OpenAPI/Swagger.
